A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SON-GOKU, and their main text, equations, figures, and tables are readable and directly comparable. However, v4 includes Appendices A–S, while v5 ends after its references and points to supplementary materials that are not supplied. The omissions below concern the supplied PDFs; the contents of any separate supplement cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v4 reports original six-dataset evaluations and timing measurements in Tables 1–2, plus Taskonomy experiments and supplementary analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experimental outcomes in Tables 1–2, including baseline comparisons, scheduler ablations, and timing measurements.

M1.justification: The core procedure remains EMA-based conflict estimation, thresholding, greedy coloring, and cyclic group updates. v5 clarifies that EMA gradients construct the graph while current gradients update parameters, consistent with v4's equations and Algorithm 1. Renaming sketch width from r to d_sk does not change the method.

E1.justification: The six main benchmarks remain unchanged. However, the supplied v5 no longer presents v4's Taskonomy/Taskonomy Tiny evaluations, including additional dense-prediction tasks such as edge detection, keypoints, curvature, and reshading. This substantially reduces documented evaluation coverage without establishing that those experiments were abandoned.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 is unchanged; GO4Align and EXTRA are discussed but not evaluated. The omitted supplementary comparisons include SON-GOKU+TAG, a no-refresh baseline, joint training across encoder widths, and CAGrad in the expanded timing table.

E3.justification: The retained experiments show no revised settings. The supplied evaluation suite nevertheless loses substantial setting comparisons: refresh periods 4 and 256 in v4 Table 5, encoder widths 64/128/256 in Table 10, and the width-by-refresh-period timing experiment in Figure 2. These are omitted evaluation configurations, not evidence of rerunning the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Table 1's recoloring, history, and graph-construction ablations remain. v5 omits the additional analyses of sketching and approximation strategies, alternative TAG affinities, backbone capacity, resource use, and training-time conflict/group evolution documented in v4 Appendices D, N, P, R, and S.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their uncertainty values, including Table 2's standard-deviation reporting. However, v4's disclosure of ten timing repetitions is absent, alongside supplementary two-seed, five-trial, fifteen-trial, and percentile-band reporting. This is reduced statistical documentation, not evidence that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 match. Numerous supplementary results are absent, including Taskonomy validation scores, resource measurements, and convergence curves. For example, v4 Table 9 reports 193.41±6.27 ms/step for cosine SON-GOKU versus 255.29±17.84 for SON-GOKU+TAG; neither result appears in v5.

T1.justification: The main mathematical statements remain essentially unchanged, but v5 does not contain v4's detailed assumptions, definitions, theorems, and proofs in Appendices B–I. Additional formal material, including the aggregate conflict ratio, scheduled-versus-aggregated bound conditions, and signal-to-noise derivation, is also absent. No replacement proofs are supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: interference-aware graph-coloring scheduling, theoretical guarantees, improvements across six benchmarks, compatibility with existing optimizers, and the importance of recoloring and history averaging.

C2.justification: Section 7.3 more cautiously connects optimization theory to held-out gains, replacing 'theoretically generalizes' with 'can improve performance.' However, the supplied v5 also loses substantial qualifications and interpretations, including conditions under which scheduled bounds need not improve, cyclic-gradient bias, approximation failures, TAG's runtime tradeoff, and capacity-dependent benefits.

D1.justification: v5 omits the reproducibility statement, algorithm block, detailed dataset/auxiliary construction, architecture descriptions, and timing protocol. It adds optimizer-state clarification and compute-provider acknowledgements, and changes the implementation link from SON-GOKU-ICLR-95AB to SON-GOKU-Impl. The new link's contents and availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v5 adds an explicit distinction from GO4Align and EXTRA and several supporting citations. Conversely, v4's extensive related-work discussions in Appendices M and Q and numerous associated references are absent, substantially contracting the documented research context despite retaining the main four-family taxonomy.

P1.justification: The document changes from a main paper with extensive internal appendices to a main-text-only presentation referring to separate supplementary materials. The reproducibility section disappears, acknowledgements and a second author with affiliations appear, and several numbered subheadings become run-in headings. Most shared scientific prose receives only localized clarification.

P2.justification: v5 adopts narrower text blocks, running headers, and different typography and float placement. Figure 1 uses the identical image and Tables 1–2 retain their data, but Algorithm 1, supplementary Tables 3–11, and Figures 2–7 are absent, removing substantial visual evidence and explanatory displays.

improvement.justification: As supplied, v5 retains broad theoretical and empirical claims while replacing v4's proofs, important qualifications, reproducibility details, and supporting experiments with references to unavailable supplementary materials. Clearer notation and more cautious generalization language are useful but do not offset the substantial loss of assessability and reproducibility. This judgment concerns the supplied PDFs, not any separately distributed supplement.
